ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: The graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ passes through points $A(0, 2)$ and $B(-2, 0)$. Find the analytic expression of this linear function.
ready1_open_rewrite.title: MM-Math open-ended problem
ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: The graph of the linear function $y=kx+b$ passes through points $A(0, 2)$ and $B(-2, 0)$. Find the analytic expression of this linear function.
ready1_open_rewrite.expected_answer: Based on the information given in the question, we have \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} b=2 \\ -2k+b=0 \end{array} \right. \] Solving this, we obtain \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} k=1 \\ b=2 \end{array} \right. \] Hence, the equation of the linear function is \boxed{y=x+2}.

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: Based on the information given in the question, we have \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} b=2 \\ -2k+b=0 \end{array} \right. \] Solving this, we obtain \[ \left\{ \begin{array}{l} k=1 \\ b=2 \end{array} \right. \] Hence, the equation of the linear function is \boxed{y=x+2}.
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: The function has the form y=kx+b and passes through A(0,2) and B(-2,0). Substitute A(0,2): 2=k·0+b, so b=2. Substitute B(-2,0): 0=k·(-2)+b. Using b=2 gives 0=-2k+2, so 2k=2 and k=1. Therefore the analytic expression is y=x+2.
